history: The Subaru WRX STI is the pinnacle of Subaru's performance lineage, born from decades of World Rally Championship dominance. Introduced to the North American market in 2004, the STI brought the fire-breathing performance of Subaru's rally cars to public roads, wrapped in a practical four-door sedan body.

At the heart of the STI is Subaru's signature EJ257 2.5-liter turbocharged flat-four engine — a boxer configuration that lowers the center of gravity and produces a distinctive exhaust burble beloved by enthusiasts worldwide. Paired with a close-ratio 6-speed manual transmission and Subaru's legendary Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive system, the STI offered rally-bred traction in virtually any condition.

The STI's Driver Controlled Center Differential (DCCD) set it apart from competitors, allowing drivers to manually adjust the front-to-rear torque split on the fly. Combined with Brembo brakes, Bilstein dampers, and an aggressive aero package, the STI was as capable on a twisty mountain road as it was on a stage rally course.

Production of the beloved EJ-powered STI continued through 2021, when Subaru retired the model in the United States. Over its 17-year run, the WRX STI became one of the most iconic performance cars of its generation — a benchmark for all-weather performance and driver engagement that remains deeply revered by enthusiasts worldwide.
did_you_know: The STI's iconic rear wing isn't just for looks — at highway speeds it generates meaningful downforce to keep the rear of the car planted. The large Gurney flap on the trailing edge was a direct carryover from Subaru's World Rally Championship cars.

trims.name: WRX STI
trims.description: The base STI trim with the full performance package — EJ257 engine, DCCD AWD, Brembo brakes, Bilstein dampers, and the iconic rear wing.

trims.name: STI Limited
trims.description: Adds premium interior appointments including leather seating, navigation, and upgraded audio while retaining the full performance hardware.

trims.name: STI Sport
trims.description: Mid-tier trim adding Recaro front seats, a leather-wrapped steering wheel, and gloss black exterior accents over the base STI.

trims.name: STI Type RA
trims.description: Record Attempt special edition limited to 500 units. Reduced weight, STI Performance exhaust, carbon fiber roof, and a Nürburgring-tuned suspension.

variants.name: STI Type RA
variants.description: A 500-unit limited edition built to set lap records. The carbon fiber roof, lightweight 18-inch BBS wheels, and STI Performance exhaust made it the lightest and most track-focused STI sold in the US.

variants.name: STI S209
variants.description: The first Subaru S-line model sold in the United States, limited to 209 units. Featured an upgraded EJ257 producing 341 hp, wider fenders, and a massive dual-element rear wing — a true collector's item.

variants.name: STI Spec C
variants.description: A Japan-market variant with significant weight reduction, revised suspension tuning, and a higher-flowing intake system. Never officially sold in North America but highly sought after by importers.
